item.title: [New] Defender for Identity's October release adds 21 alerts: AD CS ESC1/ESC8/ESC11 abuse, diamond tickets, DPAPI master key theft, Temporary Access Pass sign-in and seven Okta detections
item.description:
New alert titles arrive in the queue without a playbook, and several cover attack paths (AD CS ESC1/ESC8/ESC11, diamond tickets, CA key theft) that end in domain compromise.

MDI · Map each new alert title to a triage playbook and an owner, check the MDI sensor version and AD CS coverage the alerts need, and make sure Okta is connected if you rely on the seven Okta detections.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [Due today] Defender for Cloud Apps switches the SaaS accounts integration with Identity inventory on automatically from 15 October
item.description:
Accounts from connected SaaS applications start appearing in the Defender Identity inventory without anyone opting in, so the inventory count, identity-based hunting results and anything keyed to that inventory change on a date Microsoft chose. A tenant that still uses the two scoped Defender for Cloud Apps admin roles is excluded, which is the same pair of roles Microsoft closed to new assignments on 4 October.

Defender XDR · deadline 2026-10-15 · Before 15 October check whether the tenant uses the User group admin or App/instance admin role in Defender for Cloud Apps; if it does not, expect SaaS accounts in the Identity inventory from that date and tell the analysts who work identity incidents that the inventory will grow.

item.title: [Due today] App Governance permissions change for three Entra roles as Defender XDR Unified RBAC takes over
item.description:
Two compliance roles silently lose an app-governance capability and one security role gains it: an app-governance policy nobody can edit, or one an unexpected role can now edit, is a control gap either way.

Defender XDR · deadline 2026-10-15 · Before mid-October, list who reaches App Governance through Compliance Administrator, Compliance Data Administrator or Cloud App Security Administrator, review custom Defender XDR Unified RBAC roles for Defender for Cloud Apps, and reassign affected people to a supported Entra role or a custom Unified RBAC role on least privilege.

item.title: [New] Security Operator is now documented as able to disable, enable, revoke sessions and force a password change on Entra ID accounts from Defender for Identity
item.description:
Security Operator is a common SOC analyst role. If the page reflects the service, holders of it can now disable an Entra ID account, revoke its sessions or force its password change from the identity page in Defender XDR, which is a containment power and also a way to lock out an administrator.

MDI · List Security Operator assignments (including PIM-eligible) and confirm each holder should be able to disable accounts and force password changes; alert on these remediation actions in the Defender XDR action center and the Entra audit log when performed by a Security Operator.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Device tags: the DeviceTagging registry value carries only one tag, and tags set elsewhere are never written back to it
item.description:
Device groups, RBAC scoping and automation often key on tags; a script that reads the registry to decide a device's tags, or that writes several tags there, gets the wrong answer.

MDE · Check scripts and detections that read HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Advanced Threat Protection\DeviceTagging Group for tag membership and read the full set from DeviceInfo in advanced hunting instead, where DeviceManualTags, DeviceDynamicTags and RegistryDeviceTag are separate columns.

item.title: [New] File Integrity Monitoring in Defender for Servers: enabling or changing it now needs Owner and Security Admin on the subscription that holds the Log Analytics workspace
item.description:
File Integrity Monitoring is a detection control: whoever can change its rules can stop the monitoring of a registry key or a system path before tampering with it. The page now places that right at subscription Owner plus Security Admin rather than a workspace-level owner, and it now names changing the configuration, not only switching it on and off.

Azure · List who holds Owner and Security Admin on the subscription that contains the FIM Log Analytics workspace and confirm each is expected; alert on Defender for Servers settings writes (Microsoft.Security/pricings) in the Azure Activity log for that subscription; give SOC analysts who only read FIM results the Security Reader role.

item.title: [New] Defender for Endpoint publishes an AI agent support matrix and now says local AI agent discovery is activity based: an installed agent may not appear in the inventory
item.description:
A hunt that reads an empty AgentsInfo result as 'no AI agents on this estate' is now contradicted by Microsoft's own text: an agent that is installed and has not run since onboarding is not listed. The matrix is also the first place that says which agents can be blocked at run time and which are only seen.

MDE · Use the matrix's Name and Vendor values in AgentsInfo queries, and pair the AI agent inventory with the Defender Vulnerability Management software inventory when the question is which agents are installed rather than which have been observed running.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Sentinel gets an ASIM EmailEvent schema, and the ASIM parser list gains its first Agent Event parser
item.description:
An email rule written against EmailEvents covers Defender for Office 365 only. A normalised schema lets one analytic rule read a third-party gateway and Defender together, with the email authentication results as named fields. No source parser is listed yet, so today the schema is a target to build to rather than something a rule can query.

Sentinel · No action required. If a secure email gateway feeds Sentinel, check whether its connector ships an EmailEvent parser before writing new email rules against the source tables.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Defender Vulnerability Management starts covering Node.js, Python and Java packages on Windows; assessment exports grow and gain a ProductCategory field
item.description:
Every pipeline that pulls vulnerability assessment exports into a SIEM, a data lake or a ticketing tool sees more rows per device once this is on, and the new rows are components rather than installed applications. A dashboard that counts vulnerable software per device changes its number with no new exposure behind it.

Defender XDR · Record current export file sizes and ingestion times now. When the tenant is enabled, filter downloads by ProductCategory or apply Microsoft's Legacy Components Support List, and set a new baseline for any Delta integration.

item.title: [New] Defender for Office 365 starts detecting malicious URLs inside QR codes in Teams messages after delivery, and the detections reach Advanced Hunting
item.description:
A QR code was the way round URL scanning in Teams chat, because the link sits inside an image. This is the first time a QR-borne URL in Teams becomes a record a hunt can read, and the column Microsoft names for it is not in the published schema yet, so a query that names it directly may fail until the rollout reaches the tenant.

Defender XDR · No action required by Microsoft. Confirm Teams ZAP is on, and add the QR code hunt in Hunting to the Teams phishing playbook; it is written to run before and after the UrlLocation column arrives.
